narrative.overview:
The site reads like a well-prepared brief handed to someone with two minutes: plain structure, confident type, and color only where the proof lives. Every page runs on one shared system: proof before promise. A recruiter's eye lands on the name and role, then the measured outcome drawn as a chart, then work they can open, then where the record comes from. Nothing decorative competes for that path. The tone is warm, approachable, and clear. It's a capable person explaining their work, not a product launching itself.

Surfaces are calm and cool: slate paper, white, and hairline rules. Content sits in ruled lists and ruled columns, not cards. The Ultraviolet → Azure → Cyan signal works as the system's highlighter, and it is reserved for four places: the 3px bar at the top of the page, the 96px rule under the page's title line (the tagline on home, the H1 on inner pages), the primary action (in its deep, AA-safe form), and the "after" bar of the outcome chart. Type is one self-hosted variable family, Bricolage Grotesque, whose personality comes from its width and weight axes: display lines run slightly condensed and heavy, and the hero name widens into place as it bolds. On desktop, sections split into a sticky heading column beside the content that scrolls past it. Depth is gently layered: hairlines and tonal steps do most of the work, with two quiet shadows. Icons are drawn as 1.75-stroke line SVGs. The site is type-led: no photograph of the person appears anywhere, including link previews.

Motion has intent and a single grammar: things arrive once (the name widens, the title rule draws, headings rise from a mask, lists arrive item by item), then the page holds still. Motion arms only when the visitor allows it and script is running; with neither, every element is already visible. Light and dark themes are both first-class. Dark mode is not inverted gray. It moves to a deep violet-tinted night, with plum-to-navy washes behind the heroes and the close band.
keyCharacteristics: One signal gradient, used in four reserved places and never on text.
Calm cool neutrals. Warmth comes from voice, soft corners, and the type's character, not from color temperature.
One variable family, Bricolage Grotesque: heavy (800) display at 92% width with −0.04em tracking.
Ruled lists, ruled columns, and hairlines instead of cards and tiles.
Desktop split sections: a sticky heading column (4fr) beside the content (8fr).
Arrival motion that plays once, never blocks content, and switches off under reduced motion.
Gently layered depth: hairlines, tonal steps, and two quiet shadows.
Type-led identity: no portrait or personal photo.
Matched light and violet-night dark themes, scoped to `:root[data-theme="dark"]`.

rules.name: The Four Places Rule
rules.body: The signal gradient appears only on the top bar, the title rule (under the home tagline or an inner page's H1), the primary action, and the "after" bar. It never fills text, a background area, or a tile.

rules.name: The Deep Under White Rule
rules.body: Wherever white text sits on the signal, use the deep stops (Deep Ultraviolet → Deep Azure → Deep Cyan), never the bright ones. Accent text in light mode is Deep Ultraviolet, never Ultraviolet.

rules.name: The Mist, Not Paint Rule
rules.body: Tinted surfaces use the pale Mist tints in light mode, and the Dusk tints in dark mode. Never use a saturated fill for a surface.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Bricolage Grotesque is the only typeface on the web pages. Personality comes from its width (wdth 75–100%) and weight (200–800) axes, never from a second display face. Monospace is for inline code only.

rules.name: The Claim Is The Headline Rule
rules.body: A section opens with its H2 stating the point (for example, the outcome in plain words). There are no decorative labels or eyebrows above headings. The only labels that may sit above a heading carry information the heading cannot: the ordinal "Step n" in an ordered sequence, and a status.

rules.name: The Tabular Proof Rule
rules.body: Every number that is evidence (durations, counts, years, percentages) is set at 800 weight with tabular numerals. Dates use tabular numerals at 600.

rules.name: The Ruled Rhythm Rule
rules.body: Groups of items are rows or columns divided by rules, not cards in a grid. A list opens with a Strong Hairline above it and each row closes with a hairline below; a column opens with a 2px Ink rule.

rules.name: The Quiet Shadow Rule
rules.body: No shadow exceeds 12% opacity or a 24px blur. If depth needs to be louder than that, use a tonal step or a rule instead.

dos: Do keep the signal gradient to the Four Places: the top bar, the title rule, the primary action (deep stops), and the "after" bar.
Do build every page from the shared components (page hero, sections and split sections, ruled rows, timeline, skills, steps, case studies, close band) in `main.css` before adding a new one.
Do define every new color as a custom property on `:root` and redefine it under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`; check both themes.
Do use the deep stops or Deep Ultraviolet wherever text must be read on or as brand color.
Do keep readable text at Graphite contrast or higher in light mode (62% white or higher in dark mode), to meet the WCAG 2.2 AA requirement in PRODUCT.md.
Do present groups as ruled rows under a Strong Hairline, or ruled columns under a 2px Ink rule, with evidence numbers in tabular 800.
Do set display lines in Bricolage at 92% width, 800 weight, and −0.04em tracking; reach for the width and weight axes before any other typographic device.
Do use the split section (sticky 4fr head, 8fr body) for lists and reading passages at 1100px and wider; keep charts, case studies, and steps full width.
Do arm motion only behind `motion-ok` or `reveal-ready`, play entrances once, and give every animated element a visible final state under reduced motion and without script.
Do use the 18px, 1.75-stroke line icon set beside a text label.
Do keep `resume.html` in its own print-safe, white-background style and print scale: an Ultraviolet rule and section headings, Ink and gray text, and no gradients.
donts: Don't put a photo of the person on the site or in link previews; the og image stays type-only.
Don't show employer or client names anywhere except `resume.html`; career context lines carry role context only.
Don't put a phone number in any HTML page.
Don't fill text with the gradient, or fill large areas with the gradient or any solid brand color.
Don't add decorative labels or eyebrows above headings; the headline carries the claim. Only "Step n" ordinals and a real status may sit above a title.
Don't use emoji or icon fonts as icons.
Don't add a second typeface or another web font; Bricolage Grotesque is the one family, and the monospace stack is for inline code only.
Don't add new accent hues outside the signal's three hues and their deep stops.
Don't add heavy, dark, or colored shadows beyond the Soft Lift and Toggle Thumb.
Don't add autoplaying loops that run longer than 5 seconds; anything that moves continuously must be driven by the visitor (like the scroll-linked tool strip).
Don't let motion hide content without script: hidden start states belong only behind `motion-ok` or `reveal-ready`, never in base styles.
Don't add motion outside the grammar above, and always honor reduced motion.
